profileText: A Delegate from Maryland; born in Lancaster County, Pa., May 1, 1741; was graduated from the College of New Jersey (now Princeton University) in 1767; a signer of the declaration of freemen of Maryland; delegate to the Maryland convention of 1775; served in the Revolutionary War; appointed captain in Smallwood's Maryland Regiment January 14, 1776; joined the Continental Army in July 1776 and was promoted to lieutenant colonel of the Third Regiment, Maryland Line, December 10, 1776; taken prisoner following the Battle of Monmouth; retired from the army January 1, 1781; practiced law in Cecil County, Md., 1781-1783 and in Baltimore, Md., 1783-1790; Delegate to the Confederation Congress, 1786 and 1787; appointed United States marshal for Maryland by President George Washington, 1790 to 1798; naval officer of the port of Baltimore, Md., 1794-1817; died on October 23, 1817, in Baltimore, Md.; interment in the burial ground of the First Presbyterian Church.
